claims.title: How can a power series represent the uniformizer to a prescribed depth?
claims.hypotheses: Fix a finite local field K over ℚℓ, its residue Witt ring W, a uniformizer with separable monic Eisenstein polynomial P, and the compatible coefficient prism and period evaluations. Fix a nonnegative precision n.
claims.statement: A scaled uniformizer has an integral lift at depth n, compatible with de Rham evaluation and with every pair of maps to any common prism after pair-dependent denominator clearing.

claims.title: How does one uniformizer lift supply a whole coefficient matrix?
claims.hypotheses: Keep the coefficient and period rings at a common depth n, and take any finite rectangular matrix of integral coefficients.
claims.statement: One common power of ℓ and an integral matrix approximate all coefficients in the de Rham filtration. For each pair of prism maps one exponent controls all coefficient differences.

claims.title: Which integral lattice do the lifted columns generate?
claims.hypotheses: Let S=W[[u]] over a complete discrete valuation Witt ring, with Eisenstein element E, and Y any finite d by m integral matrix. Fix n≥0.
claims.statement: There are integral matrices with XX′=ℓ^c E^n I, X=YQ+E^n H and XQ′=ℓ^c Y. Their columns generate the same ℓ-saturation as the input lattice im(Y)+E^n S^d.

claims.title: Why does the exponent of column i equal N − hi?
claims.hypotheses: Let UU′=I over the de Rham field. Suppose U has poles of order at most N, UCβ=I, C is integral, the columns of UC have degrees at least h_i and the rows of β at least −h_i, with |h_i|≤N.
claims.statement: Integral matrices X,X′ have scalar product ℓ^c E^(2N)I and place both UX and X′U′ in filtration degree N.

claims.title: How does Frobenius act on a basis of crystalline periods?
claims.hypotheses: Let K be a finite extension of ℚℓ and V a crystalline representation of rank d with a chosen basis, compatible local period data and a stable lattice.
claims.statement: An invertible invariant crystalline matrix gives Frobenius and inverse Frobenius coefficient matrices over the unramified field. They admit one common integral Witt scaling.

claims.title: How can the period matrix and its inverse be made integral at the same height?
claims.hypotheses: Use the crystalline invariant basis, its filtered comparison, a stable integral lattice and compatible local period data.
claims.statement: One can choose a common height, two integral changes of lattice with universal pairwise no-pole comparison, and integral crystalline period lifts with the prescribed divisibility on both sides.

claims.title: Why can the initial Galois correction be the identity on the entire disc?
claims.hypotheses: Use the integral crystalline period pair with the compatible primitive element, disc, Frobenius and Galois actions.
claims.statement: On the coefficient disc the normalized period columns have identity correction for every compatible action. The resulting integral frame has correction congruent to the identity modulo the evaluated variable.

claims.title: How does the same change of lattice compare two prism maps?
claims.hypotheses: For integral modification matrices with the three basis identities and compatible lifted coefficients, fix any two maps of the coefficient prism into any common target.
claims.statement: One exponent J for the chosen pair makes every entry of ℓ^J f(X′)g(X) divisible by f(E)^(2N).
